texts.preamble: Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 January, 2022 Author: Virender Singh Bench: Virender Singh 1 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Crr-3608-2021 (Sanjay vs The State of M.P.) Jabalpur, Dated 28-01-2022. Heard through video conferencing
texts.facts: The suspension is pleaded primarily on two grounds; that the petitioner was deprived of exercising his right under Section 13 (2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act due to more than 10 Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 January, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138940043/ 1 months' delay in filing the charge-sheet and that the manufacturer and dealer were not prosecuted by the complainant while the petitioner was only seller of the Article and he sold the sealed article; therefore, his conviction and sentence is not sustainable.
texts.arguments: 3. To substantiate his pleas, the learned Senior Counsel has placed reliance on Vitthal S/o Shankar Rao v. State of M.P. [2004 SCC Online 237], Prem Chand v. State of Haryana [2020 (4) SCC 1772 (SC)] and Alkem Laboratories Ltd. v. State of M.P. and another [2020 (2) CCSC 671 (SC)]. 4. But it is undisputed that the petitioner has never availed or exercised his rights under Section 13 (2) of the PFA and that even in absence of manufacturer or dealer, the petitioner alone can be prosecuted and until and unless it is proved that the article was sold in the same conditions as he purchased it from license holder with a written warranty in prescribed form, he cannot claim exoneration from criminal liability. In this regard we can refer to Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram (AIR 1967 SC 970) (paragraph 4), Tulsiram v. State of Madhya Pradesh [(1984) 4 SCC 487], Prabhu v. State of Rajasthan [1994 Supp (2) SCC 177], T.V. Usman v. Food Inspector, Tellicherry Municipality, Tellicherry [(1994) I SCC 754] and Gulab v. State of Madhya Pradesh [2008 (3) MPHT 131] (paragraphs 14 to 21). 6.
